is one step of the activity. It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of
questions. The full explanations, examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary comparison-criteria reliable-source market-share developer-account app-review fragmentation >}}

## 16.1 Criteria and reliable sources

- **Criteria:** the points you compare, chosen for the decision: reach,
  costs, tools, testing, review, updates.
- **Reliable source:** a known author or organisation, a **date**, its
  data. Best for a platform fact: the **maker's official page**.
- Weak: forum posts without a date, pages that sell something, old blogs.

![Criteria and sources.](images/criteria-sources.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/source-check.html" poster="sims/source-check.png" title="Source Check: can you trust this source?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The first search result is often an advertisement or an old page.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Judge five sources"}
Judge all five sources in **Source Check**. Then write at least five
criteria for your own comparison.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Sources"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the first search result|any blog"}
Which source is best for Apple's account fee?
:   Apple's developer page, with this year's date

A forum post has no author and no date. Do you use it?
:   no, find a better source

A page sells phone cases. Is it a reliable source?
:   no, it sells something

A market report shows its method and its date. Do you use it?
:   yes, with its date
:::
:::

## 16.2 The comparison table

- One **row** per criterion; one **column** per platform; a **source
  (date)** column.
- Short, exact cells: "25 USD once", not "cheaper".
- Facts that change (shares, fees) always get a date.

![A comparison table.](images/comparison-table.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"Better" and "good" are opinions. Keep them for the recommendation.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build your table"}
In Word or Excel, make the table: criterion, Android, iOS, source (date).
Fill at least five rows.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The table"}
Choose the best cell.

::: {.match extra="cheaper|Android is better"}
Account cost on Google Play?
:   25 USD once

Build machine for iOS?
:   a Mac with Xcode

Reach of Android worldwide?
:   about 70 % (report, month, year)

Which column does every line need?
:   source (date)
:::
:::

## 16.3 A recommendation

- Say **what** to do, **why** (two or three facts from the table) and
  **what would change it**.
- Fit the studio: its computers, budget and players.
- Example: "Android first: only Windows PCs, budget-phone players, 25 USD
  once. Add iOS when we have a Mac."

![From the table to the advice.](images/recommendation.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Every "because" needs a fact from your table.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Write your advice"}
Write three to five sentences of advice for Pocket Quest. Underline the
facts from your table.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The advice"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Android is the best|nothing"}
Which three parts does a good recommendation have?
:   what, why and what would change it

Byte Bay buys a Mac. Which part of the advice changes?
:   the iOS part

Where do the reasons of the advice come from?
:   facts in the table

What is wrong with "Android is the best"?
:   it gives no reason
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Fact or Myth? {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Rami's table has six lines from the Internet. For each line, decide: a fact
with an official source, a fact that changes and needs a dated report, or a
myth to remove.

{{< sim file="sims/fact-or-myth.html" poster="sims/fact-or-myth.png" title="Fact or Myth?: check the lines of the table" kind="game" height="520" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The lines"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="a fact without a source|an opinion to keep"}
“An iOS build needs a Mac with Xcode.”
:   a fact, with an official source

“Android games are always slower than iPhone games.”
:   a myth

“About 7 in 10 phones run Android.”
:   a fact that changes, with a dated report

“iPhones cannot get viruses.”
:   a myth
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Check yourself (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the newest blog|keep it as it is"}
A blog from 2019 gives a fee. What do you do?
:   check the official page today

Two sources give different shares. Which do you use?
:   the newer report that shows its data

Which word in a claim is a warning sign?
:   always

Why write the date of every source?
:   facts like fees and shares change
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Choose the criteria first, for the decision you must make.
- Use reliable sources: official pages and dated reports with data.
- A comparison table: one row per criterion, a source and a date for every
  line.
- A recommendation says what, why (facts) and what would change it.
